OK-2026-SB1451.aiSummary: The measure changes Oklahoma voter registration forms by adding a place for people to list prior voter registration in another county or state. It also says a signed registration form counts as a request to cancel any old registration, and county election boards must cancel a voter’s registration after getting notice of a new registration in another county or state. It also requires the state election board to send out a yearly electronic report with counts of certain voter registration notices and cancellations.

OK-2026-SB1437.aiSummary: The measure would direct the state Education Department to set rules for schools to give students a Presidential Fitness Test and base those rules on federal fitness advice. School districts would have to give the test once the rules are in place, with training for staff, exemptions for some students, and a parent or guardian opt-out option. Schools would use the results to encourage daily exercise and healthy habits, and the law would take effect November 1, 2026.

OK-2026-SB1360.aiSummary: Oklahoma would change math instruction rules in public schools and create an Office of Mathematics Improvement in the State Department of Education. It would give teachers access to training, set rules for student math screening, and require schools to use a screening tool starting in the 2027-2028 school year. The measure would also change how math money is sent to districts and add funding for intervention services and district math improvement incentives. It was approved by the governor.

OK-2026-SB904.aiSummary: The bill would bar state money, Medicaid coverage, and state buildings or facilities from being used for gender transition procedures for minors. It would also say that people already getting this care can keep receiving it if it started before the law takes effect. A state officer or employee who knowingly breaks the rule could be charged with a misdemeanor, and the law would take effect November 1, 2026.
